company.name: Coalesce.io
company.industry: Data transformation SaaS for the Snowflake ecosystem

routing_rationale: Operator-VP-Engineering with engineering-economist thinking style. 13 months in role. Owns the SOC 2 program operationally inside engineering. The Senior DevOps EMEA job spec he authored explicitly requires SOC 2 adherence — confirms the compliance program lives inside his org and competes with integration work for the same scarce hours.

research_summary.trigger_event: Senior DevOps EMEA job posting (active on Ashby) explicitly requires SOC 2 adherence experience. Combined with two acquisitions in 13 months (CastorDoc March 2025, SYNQ March 2026), this signals the compliance program operationally located inside engineering competing for the integration-work hours.
research_summary.key_insight: Mike publicly tracks tooling cost-per-PR ($55/review on Claude Code → $40/seat Cursor bugbot switch). Engineering-economist frame is his vernacular. Implicit Drata/Vanta differentiation lives in 'controls continuously valid, not collected after the fact' — names what the compliance-automation category actually does (collect evidence) and what it leaves behind (control validity).

draft.body:
Two acquisitions in thirteen months expand both the integration backlog and the compliance surface — the Senior DevOps EMEA hire with SOC 2 adherence as a hard requirement is one place that lands.

Every sprint hour spent assembling SOC 2 evidence is a sprint hour not spent on the integration in flight. Transilience generates the evidence as a byproduct of how the cloud runs — the controls are continuously valid, not collected after the fact.

How is the compliance workload currently split between DevOps and the rest of the team?
draft.architecture: diagnostic — structural pattern (acquisitions expand both backlog and compliance surface), confirmation by public artifact (job spec), cost frame in his vocabulary, then question

verdict_history.reason: Opener decoded Mike's own job spec for him.

User-level review: (a) same four-item product line as Satish/Justin, (b) 'compliance surface' in subject is vendor jargon, not engineer vocabulary, (c) 'where that math shows up' had residual presumption.

Subject reset to engineer vocabulary ('SOC 2 after two acquisitions'). Frame-specific product line (controls continuously valid, not collected after the fact). 'One place that lands' replaces presumption. Conditional on dropping 'Curious' CTA prefix that echoed across drafts.
'Curious' dropped from CTA. No remaining cross-draft fingerprints.

witness.what_works: Subject lives in Mike's vocabulary — SOC 2 in sprint-hour-cost terms, not vendor-coded 'compliance surface'. Sprint-hour cost framing matches his publicly tracked engineering-economist thinking. Product line implicitly differentiates from Drata/Vanta-class compliance-automation tools without naming them. Open-question CTA invites a one-line workload-distribution answer.
witness.what_fails: Lowest-risk of the three rewritten drafts. The product line edges toward category-positioning ('not collected after the fact') but the framing is operational enough to read as observation rather than competitive jab.

review_flags: coordinate-across-coalesce-leads: sequence the four sends across at least 6 weeks
